item.dc:creator: Vincent Baus
item.description: Lead research applying data science, AI and machine learning to central banking and economic policy questions. Are you an experienced data scientist, economist or computational researcher with a strong background in data […]
item.content:encoded:
• Lead research applying data science, AI and machine learning to central banking and economic policy questions.
  • Translate innovative research into analytical tools, insights and decision-making for policy makers.
  • Provide technical leadership and build data science capability across the Bank.

Are you an experienced data scientist, economist or computational researcher with a strong background in data science techniques? Do you enjoy applying cutting-edge data science, AI and machine learning techniques to answer important economic and policy questions?

Join the Reserve Bank of Australia as a Principal Data Scientist in Economic Research, where you will work at the intersection of economics, data science and public policy, leading innovative research, collaborating with economists and policymakers, and helping shape the application of AI and machine learning in central banking.


About the team

The Data Science Hub, part of the Economic Research Department, is the hub of a vibrant and growing data science community at the Bank. Our work spans policy-relevant research, experimentation with emerging analytical techniques, and the development of tools that support economic analysis and decision making. We are building collaborations with economists, policymakers, technologists and researchers across Australia and internationally.


About the role

As a Principal Data Scientist at the Reserve Bank of Australia, you will play a leading role in advancing the Bank’s research agenda through the application of data science and AI. You will investigate complex economic and financial questions using traditional and non-traditional data, contribute to research that informs policymaking and help identify new opportunities for data science to deliver outcomes across the Bank.

Alongside your research contributions, you will provide technical leadership within the Data Science Hub, mentor staff and help translate promising research into analytical capabilities.


What You’ll Do

  • Lead and contribute to innovative research applying data science, AI, machine learning and non-traditional data to central banking and economic policy questions.
  • Collaborate with economists and policymakers to develop new approaches for analysing the economy, financial system and broader policy issues.
  • Publish and communicate high-quality research both internally and externally.
  • Translate research outcomes into analytical tools, models and capabilities that support decision making across the Bank.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentoring to data scientists, researchers and analysts across the Bank.
  • Help shape the Bank’s data science, AI and analytical capabilities, including platforms, methodologies and bet practices.


About you

  • Demonstrated research capability in data science, economics or a related quantitative field.
  • Strong technical expertise in modern data science and AI methods, including machine learning, statistical modelling, natural language processing, large language models, and associated tools and platforms.
  • Experience applying quantitative methods to complex real-world problems in economics, finance, public policy, business, computational social science, or related fields.
  • Experience producing high-quality research outputs, such as publications, working papers, technical reports, conference or workshop presentations, or other significant analytical contributions.
  • Ability to work effectively across disciplines, bringing together expertise from economics, data science, and policy.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to non-technical and senior audiences.
  • Experience leading research initiatives, mentoring colleagues and contributing to a collaborative research culture.
  • Familiarity with macroeconomics, financial markets, financial stability, monetary policy frameworks or related areas is highly regarded.
  • A research‑focused postgraduate qualification (e.g. PhD or Master’s by Research), or equivalent research experience, is strongly preferred.


Be More
Working for an organisation that truly makes a difference to the people of Australia, we can offer development and career opportunities in a collaborative environment that supports your growth, wellbeing and promotes flexibility. Your individual growth and success drives the RBA forward as an organisation. Be more means you can do more, for yourself and for Australia.

Why RBA?

The RBA makes an important contribution to the Australian economy through the pursuit of national economic policy objectives and associated activities in financial markets and banking. We also issue Australia’s banknotes and operate infrastructure critical to the payments system, all of which contribute to the welfare of the Australian people.

Made up of specialists across a wide range of fields, our people, values, and culture play a critical role in achieving our objectives. Striving to be Open & Dynamic, we consider and incorporate different perspectives, work across teams and are transparent with each other, whilst delivering quality together effectively and focusing on outcomes by prioritising, testing, learning, and refining as we go.

Our people conduct themselves with a high degree of integrity, while striving for excellence in the work they perform and the outcomes they achieve. We encourage intelligent inquiry, and we treat one another with respect while promoting the public interest through our efforts. We know it is the growth and success of our people that drives the RBA forward.

Come and make a bigger contribution while you build and develop your own skills too, because being more means you can do more, for yourself and for Australia.

The Reserve Bank of Australia is committed to equity, diversity and inclusion through key initiatives. We welcome and encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, culturally and linguistically diverse background, those living with a disability and from the LGBTQ+ community. We are committed to making the recruitment process fair and equitable for all our candidates.

Application Close :

October 27, 2026

item.title: Daffodil Centre Research Fellow / Senior Research Fellow
item.dc:creator: Vincent Baus
item.description: Full-time, 2-year fixed-term opportunities (with a possible 1-year extension) at the Daffodil Centre, based in Moore College (Camperdown campus) Join the Daffodil Centre as either a Research Fellow or Senior Research Fellow, and use your expertise, research leadership and national profile to deliver high-quality cancer research with a population focus Academic Level B $132,533 – […]
item.content:encoded:
• Full-time, 2-year fixed-term opportunities (with a possible 1-year extension) at the Daffodil Centre, based in Moore College (Camperdown campus)
  • Join the Daffodil Centre as either a Research Fellow or Senior Research Fellow, and use your expertise, research leadership and national profile to deliver high-quality cancer research with a population focus
  • Academic Level B $132,533 – $157,381 or Academic Level C $162,347 – $187,198 + 17% superannuation

About the opportunity

The Daffodil Centre is a world-leading research centre, directly influencing policy decisions and real-world public health and clinical practice. The Centre is a partnership that combines the complementary strengths of the University of Sydney and Cancer Council NSW to accelerate progress in cancer prevention, early detection and cancer outcomes across the population. The partnership has created an unparalleled centre of national and international research excellence where research results in real-world improvements to reduce the burden from cancer in the community. Join the Daffodil Centre at the University of Sydney and contribute to research that is shaping the future of cancer control in Australia and internationally. Either as a Research Fellow or Senior Research Fellow, you will bring recognised expertise and an established research profile to an environment where research excellence is translated into meaningful outcomes for policy, practice and communities.

Working with a high degree of autonomy and under broad direction, you will lead impactful research, pursue competitive funding opportunities, build strategic partnerships and provide expert advice within your area of expertise, ideally related to cancer prevention or early detection with a population focus. You will play an important role in strengthening the Centre’s research standing and influence, while mentoring emerging researchers and contributing to its broader strategic, academic and governance priorities. This is an opportunity to build on your national reputation for research excellence, expand your influence within your discipline and contribute to the Daffodil Centre’s mission to deliver research that makes a real difference to cancer control.

We would like to hear from early- or mid-career researchers who have completed a PhD related to public health, epidemiology, health services research, health economics, biostatistics, implementation science, behavioural science, health policy or clinical fields. Experience working with priority populations as defined in the Australian Cancer Plan will be highly regarded. Mentoring and career development opportunities will be provided.

A description of the Daffodil Centre and its teams is available on the Centre website . Have a preference for a certain research project and/or research team? Feel free to specify within your application when applying for the role.

Your key responsibilities as an Academic Level B Research Fellow:

  • Conduct high-quality original cancer research independently and collaboratively, contributing to publications, conference presentations and competitive research funding applications.
  • Build and maintain a strong research profile through peer-reviewed publications, conference and seminar presentations, and other scholarly outputs.
  • Develop research collaborations and contribute to translational research that informs policy and practice and delivers meaningful outcomes for the community, profession and government.
  • Contribute to the development of competitive research grant applications and research activities that generate impact and support the strategic priorities of the Daffodil Centre and University.
  • Provide training, informal mentoring and guidance to colleagues and postgraduate research students, where appropriate, while contributing to a positive, collaborative and inclusive research culture.

    • Develop productive relationships with research partners, government, industry and other external stakeholders, contributing expertise to forums, seminars, conferences and public debate.

In addition to the above, as an Academic Level C Senior Research Fellow:

  • Establish and nurture partnerships and collaborations that support cancer research and deliver meaningful outcomes across policy, practice and research.
  • Mentor and support early-career researchers, contributing to a collaborative culture of academic excellence, inclusion and innovation.

    • Contribute to the Centre’s research, governance and strategic priorities, including academic committees, community engagement and activities that strengthen the impact and profile of the Daffodil Centre.

About you as an Academic Level B Research Fellow:

  • Completed PhD, with demonstrated expertise in cancer research methodologies, design and delivery.
  • A developing research profile, with evidence of original research, scholarly publications, presentations and/or other research outputs relevant to your discipline or area of expertise.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and collaboratively, applying sound judgement to research activities and providing informed advice and recommendations.
  • A developing network of academic, government, and professional partners and stakeholders, with strong communication and relationship-building skills.

    • Proven experience in planning and organising research activities, as well as supervising, mentoring or supporting colleagues and/or research students where appropriate.

In addition to the above, as an Academic Level C Senior Research Fellow:

  • A proven track record of research leadership, with the ability to develop influential research programs and contribute to expanding knowledge and practice.
  • Significant experience supervising and mentoring researchers, with a commitment to supporting the development of emerging academic talent.

    • An established network across academic, government, and professional institutions, partners and stakeholders, with the ability to leverage these relationships to strengthen research collaboration and impact.

Pre-employment checks and declarations

Your employment is conditional upon the successful completion of all pre-employment or background checks required for the role in terms satisfactory to the University. Also, to meet the University’s obligations under the National Higher Education Code to Prevent and Eliminate Gender-Based Violence you will be asked to declare if you have been investigated for, or found to engaged in, sexual harm or gender-based violence in the course of previous employment or in a legal process. Similarly, your ongoing employment is conditional upon the satisfactory maintenance of all relevant clearances and background check requirements. If you do not meet these conditions, the University may take any necessary step, including the termination of your employment.

EEO statement

At the University of Sydney, our shared values are trust, accountability and excellence and we strive to be a place where everyone can thrive. We are committed to creating a University community that thrives through diversity and reflects the wider community that we serve. We deliver on this through our commitment to diversity and inclusion , evidenced by our people and culture programs, as well as key strategies to increase participation and support the careers of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander People , women , people living with a disability , people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds , and those who identify as LGBTQIA+ . We welcome applications from candidates from all backgrounds.

We are proud to be recognised as an Australian Workplace Equality Index (AWEI) Platinum Employer. Find out more about our work on diversity and inclusion .

How to apply

Applications (including a cover letter, CV, and any additional supporting documentation) can be submitted via the Apply button at the top of the page. In your cover letter (no more than 2 pages), please outline your research area of interest and proposed research ideas for the Fellowship, and how it would fit with the Daffodil Centre.

For employees of the University or contingent workers, please login into your Workday account and navigate to the Career icon on your Dashboard. Click on USYD Find Jobs and apply.

For a confidential discussion about the role, or if you require reasonable adjustment or any documents in alternate formats, please contact Roshik Prasad, Recruitment Operations by email to roshik.prasad@sydney.edu.au

© The University of Sydney

The University reserves the right not to proceed with any appointment.

Click to view the Level C Senior Research Fellow Position Description .

Click to view the Level B Research Fellow Position Description .

item.content:encoded:
Classification: Academic Level B or C

Salary package: $124,638 – $166,338 per annum plus 17% superannuation
Terms: Full time, Tenure Track

Position overview

The Research School of Economics at the Australian National University (ANU) is seeking expressions of interest from highly qualified candidates for the position of Lecturer or Senior Lecturer in Economics specialising in econometrics or empirical economic research, however any field of specialisation will be considered. The successful candidates must currently hold a PhD or have submitted a PhD in the discipline of Economics. The successful applicants will complement and extend existing research and teaching strengths within the ANU Research School of Economics and will be committed to high-quality teaching and excellence in research.

Several tenure track positions are available. Tenure track appointments will be for an initial period of seven years, with the option of renewal or conversion to an ongoing position at the end of the initial employment agreement in accordance with the ANU Enterprise Agreement.

Position location

The ANU Research School of Economics is one of Australia’s premier academic institutions and provides an outstanding environment for economic research, teaching, and research training. The successful applicant will join a strong team of academics who publish in top international journals, hold external competitive grants, and receive recognitions for their sustained pursuit of educational and research excellence.

The College

The ANU College of Business and Economics (CBE) seeks to advance knowledge through high quality teaching and research. We contribute to associated professions, industry and government by conducting world-class, long-term strategic research, and through the provision of a range of specialised undergraduate and postgraduate degree programs.

As a part of Australia’s leading university, CBE provides an excellent educational experience for our students. Our global alumni network reaches the world’s leading companies, policy agencies and universities.

We strongly believe that the way in which we operate is defined by our Values and Behaviours and encourage you to apply if you are looking for a workplace that encourages respect, collegiality and excellence.

The University actively encourages applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. For more information on employment opportunities, contact our Indigenous Employment Consultant on indigenous.employment@anu.edu.au

ANU values diversity and inclusion and is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to those of all backgrounds and identities. For more information about staff equity at ANU, visit https://services.anu.edu.au/human-resources/respect-inclusion

For more information, please contact Andy Martin, School Manager: andrew.martin@anu.edu.au

Application information

  • Job market paper/recent publication
  • A cover letter detailing your motivation to apply to the RSE, ANU
  • A current curriculum vitae (CV)
  • Letters of reference (3)

Please submit your application via Econ Job Market: https://econjobmarket.org/positions/12610. All applicants will be considered for both academic Level B and C positions.

Applications which do not address the selection criteria may not be considered for the position.

Please note: The preferred candidate will be required to complete mandatory pre-employment declarations and background checks relevant to the role they have applied for, in accordance with the Background Checking Procedure and the National Higher Education Code to Prevent and Respond to Gender-Based Violence.

item.content:encoded:
DESCRIPTION

Amazon Economics is seeking Structural IO Economist (STRUC) Interns who are passionate about applying structural econometric methods to solve real-world business challenges. STRUC economists specialize in the econometric analysis of models that involve the estimation of fundamental preferences and strategic effects. In this full-time internship (40 hours per week, with hourly compensation), you’ll work with large-scale datasets to model strategic decision-making and inform business optimization, gaining hands-on experience that’s directly applicable to dissertation writing and future career placement.

By applying to this role, you are automatically being considered for all our available STRUC internships in 2027.

Key job responsibilities
As a STRUC Economist Intern, you’ll specialize in structural econometric analysis to estimate fundamental preferences and strategic effects in complex business environments. Your responsibilities include:

  • Analyze large-scale datasets using structural econometric techniques to solve complex business challenges
  • Applying discrete choice models and methods, including logistic regression family models (such as BLP, nested logit) and models with alternative distributional assumptions
  • Utilizing advanced structural methods including dynamic models of customer or firm decisions over time, applied game theory (entry and exit of firms), auction models, and labor market models
  • Building datasets and performing data analysis at scale
  • Collaborating with economists, scientists, and business leaders to develop data-driven insights and strategic recommendations
  • Tackling diverse challenges including pricing analysis, competition modeling, strategic behavior estimation, contract design, and marketing strategy optimization
  • Helping business partners formalize and estimate business objectives to drive optimal decision-making and customer value
  • Build and refine comprehensive datasets for in-depth structural economic analysis
  • Present complex analytical findings to business leaders and stakeholders


BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3rd year or greater PhD student in Economics or related field


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Knowledge of data analysis languages (e.g., R, Stata, Python, etc.) or other statistical software

DESCRIPTION

Amazon Economics is seeking Reduced Form Causal Analysis (RFCA) Economist Interns who are passionate about applying econometric methods to solve real-world business challenges. RFCA represents the largest group of economists at Amazon, and these core econometric methods are fundamental to economic analysis across the company. In this a full-time internship (40 hours per week, with hourly compensation). You’ll work with large-scale datasets to analyze causal relationships and inform strategic business decisions, gaining hands-on experience that’s directly applicable to dissertation writing and future career placement.

By applying to this role, you are automatically being considered for all our available RFCA internships in 2027.

Key job responsibilities
As an RFCA Economist Intern, you’ll specialize in econometric analysis to determine causal relationships in complex business environments. Your responsibilities include:

  • Analyze large-scale datasets using advanced econometric techniques to solve complex business challenges
  • Applying econometric techniques such as regression analysis, binary variable models, cross-section and panel data analysis, instrumental variables, and treatment effects estimation
  • Utilizing advanced methods including differences-in-differences, propensity score matching, synthetic controls, and experimental design
  • Building datasets and performing data analysis at scale
  • Collaborating with economists, scientists, and business leaders to develop data-driven insights and strategic recommendations
  • Tackling diverse challenges including program evaluation, elasticity estimation, customer behavior analysis, and predictive modeling that accounts for seasonality and time trends
  • Build and refine comprehensive datasets for in-depth economic analysis
  • Present complex analytical findings to business leaders and stakeholders


BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3rd year or greater PhD student in Economics or related field


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Knowledge of data analysis languages (e.g., R, Stata, Python, etc.) or other statistical software

item.dc:creator: Vincent Baus
item.description: Make your mark for patients We are looking for a Health Economics & Outcomes Research Strategy Lead who is strategic, analytical, and influential to join our Patient Evidence team, helping shape global evidence strategies that support successful payer, HTA, and reimbursement outcomes for UCB’s portfolio based in Brussels, Belgium; Slough, UK or Monheim, Germany. About […]
item.content:encoded:
Make your mark for patients

We are looking for a Health Economics & Outcomes Research Strategy Lead who is strategic, analytical, and influential to join our Patient Evidence team, helping shape global evidence strategies that support successful payer, HTA, and reimbursement outcomes for UCB’s portfolio based in Brussels, Belgium; Slough, UK or Monheim, Germany.


About the Role

As HEOR Strategy Lead, you will be responsible for developing and executing global Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR) strategies aligned with HTA and payer evidence requirements across the product lifecycle.

You will act as a key member of the global payer sub-team, representing the HTA and payer perspective within evidence generation and clinical development activities. By identifying evidence gaps, informing development strategies, and connecting access objectives to robust evidence generation plans, you will play a critical role in enabling successful reimbursement and patient access.

This role offers the opportunity to influence strategic decisions from development through commercialization, ensuring evidence generation activities address the evolving needs of healthcare decision-makers worldwide.


Who You’ll Work With

You will work closely with colleagues across Market Access, Patient Evidence, Real World Evidence, Patient Centered Outcomes Research, Biostatistics & Quantitative Sciences, Clinical Development, and Medical Affairs. You will also collaborate with affiliate teams, external experts, and research partners to ensure evidence generation strategies support successful access outcomes.


What You’ll Do

  • Develop and continuously refine global HEOR and payer evidence strategies aligned with asset and market access objectives.
  • Design and deliver key HEOR evidence generation activities, including cost-effectiveness models, budget impact models, systematic literature reviews, indirect treatment comparisons, healthcare resource utilization studies, and quality-of-life research.
  • Develop asset value assessments and support economically justified pricing and value strategies.
  • Build and communicate compelling economic value stories for assigned assets and indications.
  • Influence clinical development programs to ensure evidence generation plans address payer and HTA requirements, including evolving EU HTA needs.
  • Represent HTA and payer perspectives within cross-functional evidence generation and development teams.
  • Support the creation of global value dossiers and guide affiliate teams on reimbursement and access strategies.
  • Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to execute studies that strengthen payer decision-making, including patient preference and natural history studies.
  • Integrate affiliate and market-specific payer requirements into global evidence generation plans.
  • Contribute to scientific publications, congress presentations, external partnerships, and thought leadership activities.


Interested? For this role we’re looking for:

  • Master’s degree or PhD in Health Economics, Market Access, Outcomes Research, Public Health, Epidemiology, Pharmacy, or a related field.
  • At least 8 years of experience within the pharmaceutical industry, including consultancy experience where relevant.
  • Strong expertise in health economic modelling, outcomes research, and payer evidence generation.
  • Experience supporting HTA submissions, reimbursement strategies, and access initiatives across key markets.
  • Experience working in global or matrix organizations, with above-country or intercontinental exposure highly valued.
  • Strong leadership, communication, stakeholder management, and strategic thinking skills.

Are you ready to ‘go beyond’ to create value and make your mark for patients? If this sounds like you, then we would love to hear from you!


About us
UCB is a global biopharmaceutical company, focusing on neurology and immunology. We are over 9.000 people in all four corners of the globe, inspired by patients and driven by science.


Why work with us?
At UCB, we don’t just complete tasks, we create value. We aren’t afraid to push forward, collaborate, and innovate to make our mark for patients. We have a caring, supportive culture where everyone feels included, respected, and has equal opportunities to do their best work. We ‘go beyond’ to create value for our patients, and always with a human focus, whether that’s on our patients, our employees, or our planet. Working for us, you will discover a place where you can grow, and have the freedom to carve your own career path to achieve your full potential.

At UCB, we’ve embraced a hybrid-first approach to work, bringing teams together in local hubs to foster collaborative curiosity. Unless expressly stated in the description or precluded by the nature of the position, roles are hybrid with 40% of your time spent in the office.

UCB is an equal opportunity employer. All employment decisions will be made without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable laws.

Should you require any adjustments to our process to assist you in demonstrating your strengths and capabilities contact us on EMEA-Reasonable_Accommodation@ucb.com. Please note should your enquiry not relate to adjustments; we will not be able to support you through this channel.

item.dc:creator: Vincent Baus
item.description: We wish to appoint a Research Associate with expertise in economics and/or health economics to join the Health Organisation, Policy and Economics (HOPE) research group at The University of Manchester. The successful candidate will join the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Policy Research Unit in Health and Care Systems and Commissioning (PRUComm). […]
item.content:encoded:
We wish to appoint a Research Associate with expertise in economics and/or health economics to join the Health Organisation, Policy and Economics (HOPE) research group at The University of Manchester. The successful candidate will join the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Policy Research Unit in Health and Care Systems and Commissioning (PRUComm).


You will be responsible for:

  • Contribute to the design, conduct and analysis of novel research as part of a multi-disciplinary team
  • Identify and critically appraise relevant academic and policy literature
  • Source, collate and clean a range of administrative and survey data on health and care spending, utilisation, and outcomes
  • Design and undertake micro-econometric analyses
  • Develop networks and productive working relationships with key stakeholders within the NHS and Department of Health and Social Care

We welcome candidates who bring diverse perspectives, experiences, and approaches to their work.


About You

We encourage applications from individuals with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. You should demonstrate:


Essential Criteria:

  • Excellent undergraduate degree (or equivalent) in Economics or a related quantitative discipline
  • Excellent Masters degree (or equivalent) in Economics or Health Economics, with a substantial econometrics component
  • Experience of applying micro-econometric techniques
  • Experience of managing and analysing complex data sets
  • Clear oral and written presentation skills, with the ability to communicate with both academic and policy audiences


Desirable Criteria:

  • PhD in Health Economics or Economics
  • Evidence of publishing in high-quality peer-reviewed journals
  • Experience of applying micro-econometric techniques for programme evaluation
  • Knowledge of the health and care system in England

We value transferable skills and real-world experience as much as formal qualifications.


This full-time post allows a mix of office-based and homeworking within the UK. The minimum expectation is that you attend the office in Manchester on a weekly basis for wider research group meetings/seminars.


Our benefits include:
Generous employer contribution pension
29 days annual leave plus bank holidays, along with Christmas closure
Ride to work and EV car scheme available

For more information, please see University of Manchester Benefits. You can also find information on our Flexible and Hybrid working here.

We are an open place of enquiry and challenge. We embrace and celebrate difference, diversity and debate, and we pride ourselves on being a place of education, learning and community where we are able, within the law, to question and test received wisdom, express new ideas and explore controversial or unpopular topics and opinions. Find out more from our Freedom of Speech Policy.

item.content:encoded:
Requisition ID # 174369

Job Category: Business Operations / Strategy

Job Level: Individual Contributor

Business Unit: Strategy & Growth

Work Type: Hybrid

Job Location: Oakland

Department Overview

Energy Policy & Procurement (EPP) secures electricity and natural gas from wholesale markets for PG&E customers to ensure system reliability. In addition, EPP is responsible for long-term planning, risk management, and compliance functions related to PG&E’s energy portfolio. EPP also actively participates in regulatory and legislative proceedings that shape the design and implementation of state, regional, and federal energy regulation and policy.

The Associate Quantitative Analyst position resides within the System Planning team. System Planning is responsible for forecasting volumes, costs, and impacts of demand- and supply-side energy resources. The team is also responsible for market assessment of supply-side and demand-side energy resources. System Planning supports long-term planning for supply-side and demand-side resources, electric transmission and distribution infrastructure, financial planning, and business strategies to meet the future energy needs of PG&E’s customers reliably, at a reasonable cost, and consistent with company and regulatory, legislative, and environmental policies.

Position Summary

PG&E is seeking a quantitative analyst to develop, analyze, and improve forecasts of customer electric demand and emerging energy technologies. The analyst will apply statistical, economic, and data-analytics methods to large and complex datasets; evaluate market, policy, and technology drivers; build reproducible forecasting tools; and communicate findings to stakeholders. This role requires strong quantitative and data-management capabilities, along with demonstrated knowledge of or interest in distributed energy resources, retail choice, and the regulated utility environment.

The California energy landscape is rapidly evolving due to converging policy, technology, and customer trends that are driving a cleaner and more decentralized energy future. The analyst will be part of a dynamic and innovative team responsible for forecasting electric demand and the impacts of emerging customer energy choices, including load-serving entity choice, building electrification, electric vehicles, energy efficiency, rooftop solar, energy storage, and data centers. The team’s forecasts are critical inputs to PG&E’s business strategy, energy supply portfolios, and infrastructure plans.

The analyst will support senior team members and stakeholders in developing data-driven forecasts of customer energy demand and technology adoption. Working with internal subject-matter experts, the analyst will evaluate market, policy, technology, and customer-usage data to develop forecast assumptions and identify emerging trends. The analyst will also create analytical and visualization tools that improve forecast production, delivery, transparency, and usability.

The successful candidate will demonstrate analytical capability, initiative, intellectual curiosity, structured thinking, strong written and verbal communication skills, and team-orientated approach.

This position is hybrid, working from your remote office and your assigned work location based on business need. The work location is Oakland, CA.

PG&E is providing the salary/pay range for this position. The actual amount paid to an individual will be based on multiple factors, including, but not limited to, internal equity, specific skills, education, licenses or certifications, experience, market value, and geographic location. The range to reasonably expect will be between the minimum to the midpoint of the range. The final decision will be made on a case-by-case basis related to the factors above. This job is also eligible to participate in PG&E’s discretionary incentive compensation programs.

Bay Area Minimum: $73,000.00

Bay Area Midpoint: $91,000.00

Bay Area Maximum: $109,000.00

Job Responsibilities Forecasting Analysis : Frame and execute quantitative analyses supporting forecast inputs, assumptions, scenarios, and uncertainties for customer demand, retail choice, and behind-the-meter technologies. Develop analytical tools in collaboration with team members. Assess relevant market, policy, economic, and technology trends. Deliver forecast results and summarize methods, findings, limitations, and implications for technical and nontechnical stakeholders. Data Management and Visualization : Acquire, extract, clean, integrate, validate, document, and analyze large datasets related to energy technologies, customer demographics, customer decisions, and energy-use patterns. Develop reproducible workflows and share approaches and findings with team members. Build visualizations and reporting tools that support forecast review, production, and delivery. Continuous Improvement : Contribute to improvements that increase the efficiency, quality, transparency, reproducibility, and usefulness of energy-resource forecasting. Research and document forecasting practices, stakeholder use cases, product requirements, analytical methods, processes, and forecast-production platforms. Project Delivery: Manage multiple assigned analytical workstreams involving partners within and outside System Planning. Establish and communicate priorities, identify risks or dependencies, and reliably deliver results consistent with agreed scope, schedule, and quality expectations.

Qualifications

Minimum: Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Machine Learning, Computer Science, Physics, Econometrics, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, Applied Sciences, Statistics, Business Analytics or equivalent field.

Desired: Demonstrated experience performing quantitative analysis relevant to energy, climate, infrastructure, technology, customer behavior, or public policy Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and experience developing clear data visualizations or analytical reporting products. Experience acquiring, cleaning, analyzing, and interpreting complex datasets Ability to communicate analytical methods, assumptions, and findings clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences Proficiency with one or more analytical programming or query languages, such as Python, R, SQL, SAS, Stata, or MATLAB Advanced degree in a quantitative discipline Experience with energy demand, technology-adoption, or customer-choice forecasting Experience with statistical, econometric, time-series, techno-economic, or scenario-analysis methods Experience working with customer energy-use, economic, or technology datasets Experience at a utility, regulatory agency, energy market participant, research organization, consulting firm, technology company, or similar organization Familiarity with California energy policy and the regulated utility environment Experience building reproducible analytical workflows, visualization tools, or forecast-production processes

Covington, Georgia

We are the people who give possibilities purpose

BD is one of the largest global medical technology companies in the world. Advancing the world of health™ is our Purpose, and it’s no small feat. It takes the imagination and passion of all of us—from design and engineering to the manufacturing and marketing of our billions of MedTech products per year—to look at the impossible and find transformative solutions that turn dreams into possibilities.

Job Description


Job Summary:
The HEOR Intern will support the Health Economics and Outcomes Research (HEOR) team in generating and disseminating evidence to demonstrate the value of Becton, Dickinson and Company’s products and solutions. This role offers an opportunity to gain practical experience in HEOR methodologies and contribute to real-world healthcare challenges.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Assist in conducting systematic literature reviews, meta-analyses, and landscape assessments to identify relevant HEOR evidence.

  • Support the development and adaptation of economic models (e.g., cost-effectiveness, budget impact) under the guidance of senior HEOR colleagues.

  • Contribute to the preparation of HEOR deliverables, including abstracts, posters, manuscripts, and internal reports.

  • Participate in data collection, cleaning, and analysis using statistical software (e.g., R, SAS, Stata).

  • Help maintain and update HEOR databases and internal resources.

  • Attend team meetings and contribute to discussions on research design, methodology, and interpretation of results.

  • Support ad-hoc HEOR projects and initiatives as needed.


Job Qualifications:

  • Currently enrolled in a Master’s or PhD program in Health Economics, Outcomes Research, Public Health, Epidemiology, Pharmacy Administration, or a related quantitative field.

  • Strong understanding of HEOR principles, methodologies, and evidence generation.

  • Familiarity with statistical software (e.g., R, SAS, Stata) and Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word).

  • Excellent analytical, research, and communication (written and verbal) skills.

  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.

  • Prior internship or research experience in a pharmaceutical, medical device, or healthcare consulting setting is a plus.

At BD, we prioritize on-site collaboration because we believe it fosters creativity, innovation, and effective problem-solving, which are essential in the fast-paced healthcare industry. For most roles, we require a minimum of 4 days of in-office presence per week to maintain our culture of excellence and ensure smooth operations, while also recognizing the importance of flexibility and work-life balance. Remote or field-based positions will have different workplace arrangements which will be indicated in the job posting.

For certain roles at BD, employment is contingent upon the Company’s receipt of sufficient proof that you are fully vaccinated against COVID-19. In some locations, testing for COVID-19 may be available and/or required. Consistent with BD’s Workplace Accommodations Policy, requests for accommodation will be considered pursuant to applicable law.

#earlycareer

To find purpose in the possibilities, we need people who can see the bigger picture, who understand the human story that underpins everything we do. We welcome people with the imagination and drive to help us reinvent the future of healthcare. At BD, you’ll discover a culture in which you can learn, grow and thrive.

We believe that when people connect in person, we learn faster, collaborate more deeply, and build a stronger culture. Join us and enjoy a culture where face-to-face collaboration supports your learning, your progress, and your success.

To learn more about BD visithttps://bd.com/careers.

item.content:encoded:
Company

Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco

Are you a motivated college graduate looking for a chance to make a difference? The Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco is hiring Research Associates to join our Economic Research team. We welcome applications for multiple positions that start in the Summer of 2027.

We are the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco — public servants with a mission to advance the nation’s monetary, financial, and payment systems to build a stronger economy for all Americans. As part of the nation’s central bank, we are committed to understanding and serving the vibrant, expansive communities of the Twelfth District, which covers the nine western states of the U.S. That means we seek and appreciate new perspectives and build opportunities to learn and grow. At the SF Fed, we approach our work with integrity and a commitment to service.

The Economic Research department is a center for innovative thinking about all aspects of the domestic and global economy. We conduct high-caliber research and provide in-depth and independent analysis to support monetary policy, supervision, and public information. We strive to conduct frontier research that informs policy. We cover a broad set of topics: Macroeconomics, Microeconomics, International, Finance, and Macro Analysis and Economic Geography.


About the Opportunity:

  • Research Associates use analytical and computer programming skills in the areas of economics, finance, and statistics to support academic research and monetary policy work by staff economists.
  • Research Associates can conduct research with multiple staff economists across all sections, providing exposure to different areas of economics and a wide range of methods.
  • Research Associates have co-authored San Francisco Fed Economic Letters with staff economists.
  • The position requires a two-year commitment and is ideal for those considering graduate studies, particularly in economics or finance.
  • Since 2020, our Research Associates have joined PhD programs at Harvard, MIT, Princeton, Stanford, Michigan, NYU, Northwestern, Boston University, Maryland, UT Austin, UC Berkeley, UCLA, UC San Diego, UC Davis, and UC Irvine, among others. Eight of those were awarded National Science Foundation Fellowships. They have also gone to complete their graduate studies at top law, business, and public policy programs or join other prestigious research and policy institutions.
  • The San Francisco Fed offers a tuition assistance program, which allows Research Associates to take several graduate and undergraduate classes in economics, mathematics, statistics, and other areas at the University of California, Berkeley, and at Stanford University.
  • All positions are in-office, based in the vibrant San Francisco Bay Area. You would be joining a large, dynamic cohort of Research Associates who share and cultivate an environment of support, teamwork, and collegiality.


What We’re Looking For:

  • Superior academic record with a minimum of an undergraduate degree, or equivalent, completed by July 2027 and includes a strong quantitative background in econometrics, statistics, math, and/or computer programming.
  • A demonstrated interest in economics or finance.
  • Excellent writing and communication skills.
  • Experience/proficiency with R, Stata, MATLAB, or Python; other computer programming experience a plus.
  • Previous work experience as a Research Assistant also a plus, but not necessary.
  • This position requires access to confidential FOMC and or/supervisory information, which is limited to "Protected Individuals" as defined in the U.S. federal immigration law. Protected Individuals include, but are not limited to, U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, and U.S. permanent residents who either are not yet eligible to apply for naturalization or who have applied for naturalization within the requisite timeframe. Individuals who need immigration sponsorship now or in the future are not eligible for this position, including students in F-1 or J-1 status.


How to Apply:

Applications must include the following (in .pdf format) to be considered:

1. a resume
2. a cover letter

3. an undergraduate transcript (unofficial is acceptable)

4. a writing sample (optional)

5. at least one letter of recommendation, sent directly by the recommender to
SF.ER.RARecruiting@sf.frb.org.

Please submit your application and supplemental information online through our Careers portal (Workday). Direct email applications are not accepted.

IMPORTANT NOTE: When asked to upload your resume on the Workday Portal, you must upload all supplementary application documents at that time. There will not be an additional prompt to upload documents 2, 3, & 4. You must upload and save your resume, then upload the supplemental documents BEFORE SUBMITTING YOUR APPLICATION. Failure to do so will result in postponing the review of your application.

We will review applications on a rolling basis and keep the position open until all roles are filled.


Additional Information:

Information about the SF Fed Research Associate position: Research Associates Program.

Information about RA opportunities throughout the Federal Reserve System: www.fedeconjobs.org.

Base Salary for this role: $80,000.00 (Location: San Francisco, CA, In-office)


We offer a wonderful benefits package including: Medical, Dental, Vision, Pre-tax Flexible Spending Account, Backup Child Care Program, Pre-Tax Day Care Flexible Spending Account, Paid Family Care Leave, Vacation Days, Sick Days, Paid Holidays, Pet Insurance, Matching 401(k), and Retirement/Pension.


We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, perform essential job functions, and receive other benefits and privileges of employment.


The SF Fed is an Equal Opportunity Employer.


Full Time / Part Time

Full time


Regular / Temporary

Regular


Job Exempt (Yes / No)

Yes


Job Category

Economics/Research Family Group


Work Shift

First (United States of America)


The Federal Reserve Banks are committed to equal employment opportunity for employees and job applicants in compliance with applicable law and to an environment where employees are valued for their differences.

Always verify and apply to jobs on Federal Reserve System Careers (https://rb.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/FRS) or through verified Federal Reserve Bank social media channels.

City: Washington DC
Company: IDB
Posting End Date: 9/25/2026 11:59 PM EST

We improve lives

The IDB Group is a community of diverse, versatile, and passionate people who come together on a journey to improve lives in Latin America and the Caribbean. Our people find purpose and do what they love in an inclusive, collaborative, agile, and rewarding environment.

About this position

The IDB Group is looking for an active graduate student to be hired as an intern under the Consultant modality.

The 2027 Winter Internship Program is a competitive paid opportunity, based in Headquarters, for university students from member countries to learn about development work and corporate management of the Bank, and to acquire work experience at the professional level through on-the-job learning.

What you’ll do

  • Prepare clear, impactful briefs and reports that communicate key insights and recommendations from behavioral projects in health, heuristics training, financial inclusion and other development sector.
  • Engage in knowledge-sharing sessions and workshops to foster a culture of innovation and continuous learning in behavioral economics, and its application to addressing global challenges.
  • Support the full cycle of behavioral interventions from diagnosis and design to evaluation and report
  • Develop practical skills in behavioral economics research and intervention design through hands-on involvement in multiple projects.
  • Conduct literature reviews on behavioral economics interventions in development projects, summarizing key findings and identifying gaps for further research.

What you’ll need

  • Education : An active graduate student in behavioral science, economics and/or psychology from an accredited University. The graduation date should be after the Internship period.
  • Languages : Fluency in English with a working knowledge of one other Bank language (Spanish, French, or Portuguese) is a plus.
  • Key Skills : Learn continuously, collaborate and share knowledge, focus on clients, communicate and influence, innovate and try new things.
  • Soft Skills : Result-driven, collaborative, innovative, client-oriented, strong communicator, self-motivated, eager to learn, and excellent time management skills.
  • Technical skills: Strong analytical skills, applying quantitative and qualitative empirical methods, and using statistical software such as STATA and R for data analysis. A solid understanding of behavioral insights is essential.

Requirements

  • Citizenship : Be a national of an IDB member country.
  • Active student : Enrolled in a graduate (master’s or Ph.D.) program as of the starting date of the internship program. The graduation date should be after the Internship period.
  • Consanguinity : Not have family members (up to the fourth degree of consanguinity and second degree of affinity, including spouse) working at the IDB or IDB Invest.
  • First job at the IDB Group : Be a first-time participant in an Internship Program held by the Bank or Inter-American Investment Corporation (“Corporation” also known as “IDB Invest”). In addition, you have not been a former staff member, Complementary Workforce (“CW”), contractor for the Bank or the Corporation, or have previously provided services to the Bank or the Corporation through a contractor or under any other contractual modality.

Notes:

  • Submit your resume, academic transcripts (official or unofficial), and university letter certifying your student status when applying.
    • If you submit an unofficial academic transcript at the time of applying, you will be requested to present an official one if moving forward.
  • Academic transcripts and university letters should be issued within the last three months.

    • For graduate students a minimum of 50% of coursework must be completed when applying.
  • Applications without the requested documentation will be disqualified.
  • Save each file in a PDF format with your name and subject.
  • DO NOT send copies of your degree certificates or other courses.
  • You must be available to work full-time (40 hours per week) from January 16th to March 15th, 2027 . These dates are fixed and cannot be modified. Interns must complete their assignments within this period.

    • If you are an international student in the U.S.A ., your work authorization is through CPT or OPT. Consult your school advisor before applying. You must be able to work 40 hours per week , many international students are limited to working part-time, depending on their academic standing.

Type of contract and duration

  • Type of contract : Intern Consultant
  • Length of contract : Two (2) months
  • Dates of the contract: January 16th to March 15th, 2027
  • Location: Washington, D.C. – United States of America

*Internship dates may be adjusted slightly to accommodate holidays.

Our culture

At the IDB Group, we work so everyone brings their best and authentic selves to work while finding their purpose. Our people consistently strive for excellence, and we recognize and celebrate the impact of their contributions. In our efforts to drive innovation, we intentionally include all voices, cultivate a sense of belonging and champion fairness. We welcome individuals from underrepresented groups to join us and share their unique perspectives. We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodation to participate in the job interview process. If you require an accommodation to complete this application, please email us at accommodations@iadb.org .

About the IDB Group

The IDB Group, composed of the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), IDB Invest, and the IDB Lab offers flexible financing solutions to its member countries to finance economic and social development through lending and grants to public and private entities in Latin America and the Caribbean.

About IDB

We work to improve lives in Latin America and the Caribbean. Through financial and technical support for countries working to reduce poverty and inequality, we help improve health and education and advance infrastructure. Our aim is to achieve development in a sustainable, climate-friendly way. With a history dating back to 1959, today we are the leading source of development financing for Latin America and the Caribbean. We provide loans, grants, and technical assistance; and we conduct extensive research. We maintain a strong commitment to achieving measurable results and the highest standards of integrity, transparency, and accountability.

About IDB Invest

IDB Invest, a member of the IDB Group, is a multilateral development bank committed to promoting the economic development of its member countries in Latin America and the Caribbean through the private sector. IDB Invest finances sustainable companies and projects to achieve financial results and maximize economic, social, and environmental development in the region. With a portfolio of $14.1 billion in asset management and 325 clients in 25 countries, IDB Invest provides innovative financial solutions and advisory services that meet the needs of its clients in a variety of industries.

item.content:encoded:
The successful candidate will be directly responsible to the Director RSDAD and Deputy Director Monetary Modelling and Analytics Unit, RSDAD, for the proper performance of his/her duties, which will include:

1. Monetary Policy Analysis

To support Monetary Council decision making by contributing to the Bank’s Monetary Policy Reports and flagship publications by;
Conducting in-depth analysis of domestic and international macroeconomic developments including but not limited to economic growth, exchange rate dynamics, financial sector developments and other global economic trends;
Preparing high quality briefing papers, policy notes and presentations for Management/Board review.

2. Economic Policy & Research

To further the Bank’s research agenda and contribute to the Bank’s intellectual leadership by:
Providing analytical support and policy advise on monetary policy, fiscal policy coordination, structural reform assessment and economic policy design;
Authoring, leading and/or contributing on internal research projects, working papers and research publications for internal and external publication;
Engaging with external stakeholders

3. Macroeconomic Modelling and Data Science

To design, develop and maintain macroeconomic forecasting models and databases by:
Utilizing forecasting models including DSGE, SVAR, BVAR and semi structural models for policy simulation and scenario analysis;
Leveraging alternative and high frequency databases to enhance economic surveillance and early warning systems
Implementing reproducible research workflows and version controlled databases
Explore the application of Natural Language Processing (NLP) and text analytics to central bank communications, market sentiment analysis and policy document analysis

4. Leadership and Collaboration

o   Espouse the Bank’s commitment to the STAR Mantra and Growth Mindset culture by:

§  Mentoring and supervising junior staff

§  Collaborating across departments

§  Represent the Bank at domestic and international engagements
